ios.name: Stim
ios.subtitle: Your development, in view
ios.promotionalText: See your development workspaces, builds and devices from your phone. Pair with your Mac to follow progress, inspect logs and control a simulator.
ios.description:
Keep an eye on your development work from your phone.

Stim connects to Stim Desktop on your Mac, where the Stim command-line tools manage your React Native and Expo workspaces. See which workspaces are running, check build progress, inspect Metro and native logs, and view the devices running your apps.

Open a live device view to inspect your app. When your Mac grants Control, you can interact with the device, type, rotate supported simulators and use their available controls.

Notifications help you return to builds and workspace activity that need attention.

Requires a Mac running Stim Desktop and stim-server. Pair your phone with that Mac and keep it reachable over your local network or configured private network. The phone app does not compile your projects itself.

macos.name: Stim
macos.subtitle: A home for development
macos.description:
See your React Native and Expo development work in one place.

Stim Desktop shows the workspaces, builds and devices managed by the Stim command-line tools on your Mac. Follow build progress, open focused Metro, native and build logs, and inspect your apps in the device viewer.

Give each workspace its own development environment, switch between devices, and use the controls supported by your simulator or emulator. Pair a phone to watch and control your work remotely.

Requires the Stim command-line tools. Local iOS development also requires Xcode; Android development requires the Android SDK. This draft describes the current desktop app, which is distributed as a notarized download outside the Mac App Store.
